## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency and regulatory compliance on GCP.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (EU and US)
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (Regional instances in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- API Gateway (Envoy)
- Video Consultation Service (MediaSoup WebRTC SFU)
- AI Symptom Checker Container (Python/FastAPI)
- E-Prescription Integration Service
- Consent & Audit Ledger
- Regional Data Store (Google Cloud Spanner / PostgreSQL)
- Async Event Bus (Google Cloud Pub/Sub)
- External Pharmacy Gateways, Identity Providers (IdP), and Payment Gateways (Stripe)

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to API Gateway: HTTPS, WebRTC, OIDC/OAuth2
- API Gateway to Internal Containers: gRPC over internal VPC
- Services to Cloud Pub/Sub: gRPC / TLS
- AI Symptom Checker to Data Store: SQL over TLS
- Platform to Pharmacy Gateways: mTLS, REST, SOAP, HL7 FHIR
- Platform to Payment Gateways: HTTPS, REST with webhooks

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Platform: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce data residency
- API Gateway: Envoy for TLS termination, routing, and rate limiting
- Video Streaming: MediaSoup (WebRTC SFU) for handling connections below 300 kbit/s
- Backend Services: Python (FastAPI) for the AI symptom checker container
- Database: Google Cloud Spanner / PostgreSQL with encryption for regional data storage
- Messaging: Google Cloud Pub/Sub for asynchronous event decoupling

## Rationale
The dual regional deployment on GCP strictly fulfills GDPR, HIPAA, and data residency constraints by isolating EU and US data. Containerizing the AI symptom checker and video SFU ensures regional regulatory traceability and high availability under unstable internet connections.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- API Gateway / BFF (Go / Envoy)
- Video Consultation Service (Node.js / WebRTC SFU / Mediasoup)
- TURN/STUN Relay Server (Coturn)
- Clinical Core & E-Prescription Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Consent & Identity Management Service (Java / Spring Security)
- Notification & Pharmacy Integration Service (Go)
- Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar (Fluentbit / Go)
- Data Storage (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Pub/Sub)
- External Systems: External Pharmacy Gateways, Identity Providers, Stripe Payment Gateways

## Relationships
- Patient/Clinician Apps -> API Gateway / BFF: HTTPS / WSS (JSON/gRPC)
- API Gateway -> Internal Containers: gRPC over mTLS (Istio Service Mesh)
- Video Consultation Service -> TURN/STUN Server: UDP/TCP (WebRTC)
- Notification Service -> External Pharmacy Gateways: HTTPS/REST (TLS 1.3)
- All Services -> Regional Cloud SQL / Cloud Storage: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / HTTPS with CMEK

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) for isolated regional data residency
- Container Orchestration: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) with Istio Service Mesh for zero-trust mTLS
- Video & Networking: Mediasoup SFU and Coturn for low-bandwidth (<300 kbit/s) resilience
- Backend & APIs: Go, Java (Spring Boot), Python (FastAPI), with gRPC and REST protocols
- Data & Messaging: Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL), Cloud Storage, and Cloud Pub/Sub for asynchronous event bus

## Rationale
Isolated regional GKE clusters ensure health data never crosses borders without explicit consent, satisfying GDPR and HIPAA constraints. Dedicated WebRTC and SFU components guarantee reliable video consultations even on unstable rural internet connections.

* Clinical Core & E-Prescription Service (Java / Spring Boot)

* Compliance Audit Interceptor -> Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar: Streams session telemetry [gRPC]

* Node.js & Mediasoup: Selected for real-time WebRTC video streaming and adaptive transcoding.
* Go & Envoy: Utilized for high-performance API routing and backend-for-frontend services.
* Java & Spring Boot: Deployed for core clinical workflows requiring enterprise security and reliability.
* Python & FastAPI: Powers the AI symptom checker to integrate seamlessly with ML ecosystems.
* PostgreSQL & Cloud Pub/Sub: Provides reliable relational data storage and asynchronous messaging.

## Rationale
The architecture strictly segregates EU and US data processing to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates while utilizing cloud-native regional deployments. Adaptive transcoding and robust SFU routing guarantee resilient video consultations for rural patients on unstable connections.

TURN/STUN Relay Server.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker across the EU and US. Ensures strict regional data residency, HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and resilient connectivity for rural patients.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- TURN/STUN Relay Server (Coturn container)
- STUN/TURN Allocation Manager (C++)
- Media Relay Engine (C++)
- Region-Bound Access Controller (Lua)
- Bandwidth Throttling & Adaptation Module (C++)
- Metrics Exporter Sidecar (Go)
- Load-Balanced Listener & Port Router (C++)
- Video Consultation Service (Node.js / WebRTC SFU)
- Consent & Identity Management Service (Java)
- Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar (Fluentbit / Go)

## Relationships
- External WebRTC Clients -> Load-Balanced Listener & Port Router: Initiates STUN/TURN requests [STUN/TURN over UDP/TCP/TLS 443/53]
- STUN/TURN Allocation Manager -> Consent & Identity Management Service: Validates HMAC time-limited tokens asynchronously [REST/HTTPS]
- Media Relay Engine -> External WebRTC Clients: Relays adaptive bitrate media streams [SRTP over UDP/TCP]
- Metrics Exporter Sidecar -> Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar: Exports relay session telemetry [Prometheus/HTTP]
- Video Consultation Service -> STUN/TURN Allocation Manager: Provisions short-term TURN auth tokens

## Technology Stack
- Coturn (C++): Core TURN/STUN engine for robust media relay under restricted firewalls
- HMAC-Based Time-Limited Tokens: Enables low-latency ICE setup without synchronous runtime bottlenecks
- Lua Scripts: Enforces strict geo-routing for regional data residency (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- Prometheus/HTTP: Collects non-PII relay telemetry for compliance auditing
- GCP (europe-west3, us-central1): Cloud infrastructure ensuring isolated regional data storage

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data isolation for GDPR and HIPAA compliance while optimizing video delivery for unstable rural connections via multi-port routing and low-latency token authentication.

Consent & Identity Management Service.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a Cross-Border Telehealth Platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. Its core purpose is to deliver secure telemedicine while enforcing strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and robust consent management.

## Key Elements
* API Gateway / BFF (Go / Envoy)
* Consent & Identity Management Service (Java / Spring Security)
* Regional Tenant Router Component (Spring Cloud / Java)
* Identity & Federation Component (Spring Security / OAuth2)
* Consent Ledger Component (Spring Data JPA)
* OPA Policy Sidecar Component (Rego / Go)
* Local Credential Cache Component (Spring Cache / Redis)
* Compliance Token Verifier Component (Spring Security JWT)
* Emergency Break-Glass Component (Java / Spring Security)
* Consent Revocation Broadcaster Component (Spring Cloud Stream / Cloud Pub/Sub)
* Audit Interceptor Component (Spring AOP)
* Data Storage (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, GCP Pub/Sub)

## Relationships
* API Gateway / BFF -> Regional Tenant Router Component: Routes identity and consent requests [gRPC over mTLS]
* Identity & Federation Component -> Compliance Token Verifier Component: Delegates token parsing and validation [In-process Java method call]
* Compliance Token Verifier Component -> Regional Tenant Router Component: Passes verified residency metadata [In-process Java method call]
* Regional Tenant Router Component -> Consent Ledger Component: Forwards localized database queries [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
* Consent Policy Engine -> OPA Policy Sidecar Component: Delegates access authorization [Local REST/UDS over mTLS]
* Identity & Federation Component -> Local Credential Cache Component: Manages user sessions [Redis protocol over mTLS]
* Consent Ledger Component -> Consent Revocation Broadcaster Component: Emits revocation notices [Spring ApplicationEvent]
* Consent Revocation Broadcaster Component -> Data Storage: Publishes revocation events [Pub/Sub over mTLS]
* Emergency Break-Glass Component -> Audit Interceptor Component: Logs override events [Spring ApplicationEvent]

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional infrastructure and data residency constraints.
* Java / Spring Boot & Spring Security: Core framework providing robust RBAC/ABAC and HIPAA/GDPR alignment.
* OPA (Rego / Go) Sidecar: Delivers low-latency policy evaluation for cross-border access control.
* Spring Cache / Redis: Caches tokens and active consent for degraded network conditions.
* GCP Pub/Sub: Propagates real-time global consent revocations.

## Rationale
This architecture uses regional service decomposition, sidecar pattern authorization, and Redis caching to enforce strict data residency while ensuring high availability. It satisfies complex international compliance frameworks (GDPR, HIPAA, EU MDR) through isolated audit interceptors and immutable consent ledgers.

Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar securely captures, sanitizes, and routes compliance logs while enforcing regional data residency.

## Key Elements
- Log Ingestion Receiver (Fluentbit Core)
- Compliance Sanitizer & Masker (Go Custom Plugin / Filter)
- Regional Dispatcher (Fluentbit Output Plugin)
- Traceability Indexer (Go Sidecar Agent)
- Buffer & Resiliency Manager (Fluentbit Mem/Filesystem Buffer)

## Relationships
- App Containers -> Unix Domain Sockets (`in_syslog`) -> Log Ingestion Receiver
- Log Ingestion Receiver -> Go-routine channels -> Compliance Sanitizer & Masker
- Compliance Sanitizer & Masker -> Go function calls -> Traceability Indexer
- Traceability Indexer -> Filesystem I/O (Fluentbit Chunk Storage) -> Buffer & Resiliency Manager
- Buffer & Resiliency Manager -> Mutual TLS (TLS 1.3 over HTTPS) -> Regional GCP Storage / BigQuery (`europe-west3` or `us-central1`)

## Technology Stack
- Fluentbit & Go: Core log ingestion and custom sanitization/traceability plugins for high performance and low overhead
- Kubernetes (GKE): Deployment as a container sidecar in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`
- Unix Domain Sockets (`emptyDir`): Zero network overhead and secure local inter-process communication
- HTTPS / TLS 1.3 (Mutual TLS): Encrypted, region-locked data egress guaranteeing regulatory compliance

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR compliance by keeping EU and US health data strictly within regional boundaries and ensuring complete AI traceability. Furthermore, local Unix sockets and persistent disk buffering guarantee system reliability and zero log loss even over unstable rural internet connections.

Data Storage.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture enforces strict regional data isolation to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates.

## Key Elements
- **Patients and Clinicians**: End-users accessing the platform globally.
- **API Gateway / Envoy (Go)**: Entry point routing incoming traffic.
- **Video Consultation Service (Node.js / WebRTC SFU / Mediasoup)**: Manages real-time video sessions with Coturn relay servers.
- **Clinical Core & E-Prescription Service (Java / Spring Boot)**: Handles clinical records and prescription workflows.
- **AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)**: Evaluates patient symptoms and recommends care urgency.
- **Consent & Identity Management Service (Java / Spring Security)**: Manages authentication and user data-sharing permissions.
- **Notification & Pharmacy Integration Service (Go)**: Handles messaging and external pharmacy communications.
- **Data Storage Containers**: Relational Data Store (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL), Object Store (Cloud Storage), Event Bus (Cloud Pub/Sub), and Audit & Traceability Store (Append-Only PostgreSQL).
- **External Systems**: External Pharmacy Gateways, Identity Providers (IdP), Payment Gateways (Stripe).

## Relationships
- **Clinical Core & E-Prescription Service -> Relational Data Store**: Reads and writes structured data via PostgreSQL Wire Protocol (TLS 1.3) using CMEK.
- **AI Symptom Checker Service -> Relational Data Store**: Reads clinical context and writes session states via PostgreSQL Wire Protocol (TLS 1.3).
- **AI Symptom Checker Service -> Audit & Traceability Store**: Logs inputs and model versions via PostgreSQL Wire Protocol (TLS 1.3).
- **Consent & Identity Management Service -> Relational Data Store**: Stores identity and consent data via PostgreSQL Wire Protocol (TLS 1.3).
- **Notification & Pharmacy Integration Service -> Data Storage**: Publishes and consumes events via Cloud Pub/Sub (gRPC/HTTPS).
- **Video Consultation Service -> Coturn Relay Server**: Handles real-time media streams via WebRTC/TURN/STUN.

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider**: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) in regions `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for data residency compliance.
- **Databases**: Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) for relational data and tamper-evident audit logs.
- **Storage**: Cloud Storage with signed URLs for unstructured medical assets and binary transfers.
- **Messaging**: Cloud Pub/Sub for asynchronous event-driven integration.
- **Security**: TLS 1.3 for data in transit; Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) partitioned via `europe-west3-kms` and `us-central1-kms`.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data residency by isolating EU and US workloads, satisfying GDPR and HIPAA requirements. The modular component design and asynchronous event bus ensure system availability even under constrained network conditions.
